claims.statement: ApprovalService (packages/server/src/services/approval-service.ts) owns the `approvals` table and its full lifecycle: rows move pending -> approved | denied | expired, and every operator surface (REST routes, dashboard, Telegram) ultimately acts through this service via ExecutionEngine.handleApprovalDecision.

createApproval() inserts the approval row, its APPROVAL_REQUESTED audit record, AND the djimitflo.approval.requested outbox event in a single db.transaction().immediate() (the required outbox event is committed by the same transaction it describes); a failing audit or outbox insert rolls the approval insert back. Only after the commit does it schedule the Telegram push, broadcast APPROVAL_REQUESTED over the WebSocket, and record a HOLD decision to the authority ledger.

The approval TTL is configurable: approvalTtlMs() reads APPROVAL_TTL_MS (default 1 hour, clamped to 5 minutes .. 7 days; non-numeric/zero/negative fall back to the default) and createApproval() sets expires_at = now + approvalTtlMs(); the requested_by maker is the requestedBy argument — the dispatcher id for engine gates, or the JWT subject for POST /api/approvals manual reviews.

decideApproval() wraps its status transition in an immediate transaction with a compare-and-swap UPDATE ... WHERE id = ? AND status = 'pending', rejects non-boolean decisions with INVALID_APPROVAL_DECISION, throws 'APPROVAL_EXPIRED' for an already-expired row and 'Approval already processed' for a decided row, persists decided_by/decided_at/decision_reason alongside the legacy approved_by/approved_at/denied_at/denial_reason fields, and writes the granted/denied audit record and the djimitflo.approval.approved/denied outbox event in the same transaction.

decideApproval enforces self-approval prevention at the data layer: when decidedBy equals approval.requested_by it throws SELF_APPROVAL_FORBIDDEN regardless of any route-level permission check, closing the maker/admin gap left open by the role table.

Expiry is lazy: getLatestPendingForTask() expires every stale pending row for a task before answering (each through expireApproval with broadcast and ledger DENY record), while decideApproval() persists the expired record and its audit inside the throwing decision transaction and raises APPROVAL_EXPIRED only after that commit.

expireApprovalRecord() cancels a task still in awaiting_approval when its approval expires, writes a task_cancelled_after_approval_expiry audit row, and is guarded so a task that already moved to another status is untouched.

Manual action reviews created via POST /api/approvals carry metadata.manual_action: true and never gate execution: getLatestPendingForTask with executionOnly: true excludes them via a json_type predicate applied before LIMIT, and ExecutionEngine.handleApprovalDecision records their decision as evidence and returns without dispatching.

recordDecision() appends every lifecycle step to the append-only authority_events ledger via recordAuthorityEvent() (sequenced per correlation_id = task id, sha-256 payload digest) with HOLD on request, ALLOW/DENY on decision, and DENY with state EXECUTION_APPROVAL_EXPIRED on expiry; recording is best-effort and returns null instead of throwing if the authority_events table is absent. Actor typing is data-driven: an actor is 'human' only when it matches a real user (users.id or users.email — the route decides as the JWT subject), 'agent:' prefix maps to 'agent', and everything else (autonomy:* rule deciders, inherit:* inherited approvals, 'system', unknown labels) maps to 'service'.

Approval lifecycle steps enqueue a djimitflo.approval.* (requested/approved/denied/expired) domain event in event_outbox as REQUIRED events: enqueueRequiredEvent() must run inside the state-change transaction (it throws otherwise) so an outbox insert failure rolls the approval change back; the insert is a no-op while EVENT_PUBLISH_ENABLED is not 'true'. EventOutboxService then drains pending/failed rows (single-flight, up to 10 attempts, 60s default interval) to DJIMIT_EVENT_BUS_URL/events/<stream> with an optional bearer token, so a bus outage delays but never loses or blocks the action.

All ApprovalService WebSocket publishes happen strictly after their commit, are filtered per-client through AuthorizationService.canReadTask by broadcastTaskEventById, and a broadcast failure is caught and logged without affecting the committed decision.

The approvals router (mounted with requireAuth at routes/index.ts L146) exposes GET list/detail with AuthorizationService task-visibility filtering (unreadable rows return 404), POST / for manual-action reviews (create:task), decision endpoints PATCH /:id and POST /:id/approve|deny behind requirePermission('approve:task') that forward to ExecutionEngine.handleApprovalDecision with decidedBy from the JWT subject (sendDecisionError maps INVALID_APPROVAL_DECISION/SELF_APPROVAL_FORBIDDEN/APPROVAL_EXPIRED/already-processed to 400/409/410/409), and POST /:id/cancel (also approve:task) which writes pending -> expired directly, returns 409 when already processed, and attributes the cancel in the audit trail (event approval.expired, action approval_cancelled).

Approval API responses are enriched by approvalContext() with goal objective, proposal title, loop run id, worker role/runtime, working directory, and a prompt preview when the task belongs to an autonomous loop run, so a worker-execution approval is distinguishable from an ordinary task review; context failures are swallowed as null.

The dashboard app shell uses usePendingApprovals to poll getAllApprovals('pending') every 30 seconds, filter past-expiry rows client-side, and refresh immediately on the APPROVALS_CHANGED window event; Layout renders PendingApprovalsBanner (urgent at <=15 minutes to expiry, linking to /decisions#approvals) on every page except /decisions, and shows the pending count as a badge on the /decisions nav item.

ApprovalQueuePage is embedded as the first section of the Decisions inbox (/approvals redirects to /decisions#approvals): it renders status tabs (pending/approved/denied/all) fed by api.getAllApprovals, guards against stale tab responses with a request-id ref, subscribes to the four approval WebSocket events (requested/granted/denied/expired) to refresh, and renders ApprovalCard rows whose Approve/Deny buttons appear only for pending rows and only when the user holds approve:task; deny opens a reason-picker dialog (fixed reason plus optional details) requiring a reason, and a decision dispatches APPROVALS_CHANGED.

Telegram acts on approvals only as an authenticated API client: TelegramApiService.request mints a JWT for the mapped user and calls a loopback-only internal API (constructor throws TELEGRAM_API_MUST_BE_LOCAL for remote URLs). TelegramBotService offers a text path (/approve, /reject -> POST /approvals/:id/approve and /deny) and an inline one-tap button flow (handleCallback), both authorized by mayApproveViaTelegram (the telegram_identities D3 mapping to an active user whose role holds approve:task) and executed through the same approval API as that user, so SELF_APPROVAL_FORBIDDEN and every other server rule still apply; a self-approve is rendered as a you-cannot-approve-your-own-request reply.

The Telegram webhook endpoint validates the X-Telegram-Bot-Api-Secret-Token header before processing, and the telegram-api-chain test drives the whole path end-to-end: webhook -> authenticated local API -> task creation -> executeTask awaiting_approval -> a mapped approver's /approve persists decided_by and runs the task to completion while a maker self-approve and a viewer approve are refused.

The decideApproval decision-guard block (approval-service.ts lines 122-145) and ToolBroker validateCapabilityToken/reevaluateOnParameterChange (tool-broker.ts 243-274) are explicit Stryker mutation-test targets in stryker.config.js with thresholds high 85, low 75, break 70.

The Telegram approval push is post-commit, delayed, and fail-soft: off unless TELEGRAM_PUSH_ENABLED, delayed by TELEGRAM_PUSH_DELAY_MS (default 15 s; 0 pushes immediately) so a lane rule that auto-approves right after creation re-checks the row as decided and skips the push; pushApproval dedupes per approval id in telegram_push_log, honors quiet hours and a TELEGRAM_PUSH_MAX_PER_HOUR cap (default 6), and never throws — the approval never depends on Telegram.
